newsitem.title: POLAND: State-owned firms among Poland's largest - survey.
newsitem.headline: State-owned firms among Poland's largest - survey.

text.p: Poland's 30 largest enterprises regarding the 1996 revenues include only six private companies, a survey by Polityka weekly published on Wednesday showed.

The survey showed that state-owned oil, energy, mining and steel companies, often loss-making, dominated the list of 30 biggest companies. Polityka, in its annual survey, published a list of Poland's 500 firms with biggest sales last year.

State-owned fuels distributor CPN SA tops the list with revenues of 11.8 billion zlotys and 131 million zloty net profit followed by oil refinery Petrochemia Plock SA with 218 million zlotys net on 10.5 billion zlotys sales.
The State Power Grid is third with revenues of 10.1 billion zlotys and 15.8 million zloty net profit.
Among the 30 biggest companies, 10 suffered losses last year, mostly coal mines and steel mills.
The copper combine KGHM Polska Miedz SA, slated for privatisation this year, is seventh on the list, with sales of 5.1 billion zlotys and 220 million zlotys net profit.
Telecoms monopoly TPSA, whose privatisation is due to start next year, is fifth with 6.7 billion zloty revenues and net profit of 850 million zlotys, the highest net among Polish companies.

Among private companies on the 30 largest firms list were the Polish unit of Italy's Fiat, Dutch-owned wholesaler Makro Cash and Carry Poland, cigarette maker ZPT Krakow owned by Philip Morris, South Korean-controlled Daewoo-FSO car maker and metal trader Stalexport.
